# Maritime ISR — demo API

The read-only serving layer for the Maritime ISR prototype: a maritime
intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance system that looks for **dark
vessels** — ships that have switched off their AIS transponder to hide — in the
Arabian Sea and Indian west-coast waters.

## Read this before believing any number it shows you

**Everything served here is synthetic.** The corpus is generated by
`maritime_isr/scenario/`, with the answers deliberately planted so the
detectors can be scored against a known truth. No real satellite scene, no real
AIS feed and no real vessel appears anywhere in it.

**No dark vessel has been detected on real data.** Not by this Space, not
anywhere else in the project. The code to do it exists and is measured against
the synthetic suite; that is a different claim, and the difference is the whole
point of stating it here.

**This is not the pipeline.** SAR preprocessing, live AIS capture and corpus
generation do not run in this container and cannot — they need persistent disk
and considerably more memory. What you are looking at is a frozen snapshot of
one local run, and it changes only when the image is rebuilt.

## What is actually in the snapshot

674 vessels across twelve behavioural archetypes, roughly 816,000 AIS position
reports, 661 built tracks, an object graph of about 2,500 nodes, and 381
generated port documents on six Indian port letterheads read back through the
real document connector.

## Access

The API token is not a security boundary and never was: the browser needs it,
so it ships in the page. Treat this Space as public, because it is. That is
acceptable only because none of the data is real.

## Speed

Warm, the heaviest endpoint answers in about 0.17 s. A free Space sleeps after
48 hours of inactivity, and the visitor who wakes it waits 30–90 seconds for
the container to start. Every visitor after that gets the warm number.
